hook: SCP-993 takes the most harmless format imaginable, a cheerful educational cartoon for small kids, and turns it into a containment problem. It is short and built around an episode guide, so it reads in a few minutes. Expect plainly stated cannibalism, murder, arson and torture in the episode summaries; their flat, TV-listing tone is what carries the chill.
whyItMatters: It is a compact take on the corrupted children's-show idea, built on one strong rule about who can and cannot see the program. Its Safe class is also a handy reminder that the label measures how easy something is to hold, not how pleasant it is: the broadcasts are simply intercepted, and the horror lives in what they would teach.
thingsToNotice:
The age rule is the clever hinge: anyone ten or older blacks out with a stabbing headache, so the only way to learn what airs is to show it to children under ten, then wipe their memories, which makes the procedure itself quietly unsettling. The episode list reads like a TV guide, and the gap between chirpy titles and contents does most of the work: Bobble kidnaps a townsman and shows how to skin, gut and cook him, burns a city building while screams play over the image, stalks and stabs a woman in London, and tortures a prisoner to death before teaching non-lethal pain.

Then the target shifts. One episode is just Bobble glaring at the viewer for thirty minutes, and the last is set in the Foundation's own video archive, where he explains how to breach containment of several anomalies and how to kill the researchers by their daily routines. An animated version of a real doctor walks past in the background at the exact time the doctor confirms he passed the archive, so the show is watching the people who watch it.
